p.i: explicarunt, quam multipliciter hominibus pecora praestent alimenta, quamquam eleganter tum lautiorum tum rusticorum mensas instruant, exornent, ac opulentent. Prima quidem illa ac innocens vita et asq; carnis inprimis desidia-ria damnauit, pecora agricultura tantum nasci exiftimans, idcoq; tam capitale erat bouem occidi, quàm ciuem, primumq; morem alimenti hominum gratia pecudes interimendi à vitiis placationibus Deorum, quae ex iis laudatiffima erant, emanasse quidam statuunt, ficq; ad posteros transfiuffe.

Caeterum ex quadrupedibus animalibus in ci-bus veniunt, menfiq; adhiberi poffunt, leo, elephantus, panthera, vrfus, camelus, equus, asinus, canis, feles, muftela, mus, mele, fcirus, erinaceus, vulpes, cuniculus, lepus, cervus, bircus, capra, pecus, ouilli, bubulus, fuillus. Quae vero ex hominis natura et temperatura magis sint familiaria ac amica, vel longius ab ea, vitaq; humaniore discedant, fuo dicetur loco, ad quem le-gatorem remitto. Hoc ἐν παραπόδῳ[?] hic, et obiter addo, esse gentem aliquam quae lupinis vescerit[?], adhuc me legisse vel audiisse non memi-nisse.
CArnes, inquit Aristoteles, & quicquid iis, simile est, in genere sanguineo sunt, cui astipulatur Galenus 2. de tem-per.

page.notes: The first word "explicarunt" begins mid-sentence, so the paragraph is a continuation. The heading "De carne generatim, notatu digna." sits on its own line. The Greek word "παραπόδῳ" is doubtful and marked [?]. "vescerit" is uncertain, as is "defida-ria" (the word split at the line end may be "desidia" or similar). The Latin word "legatorem" in "le-gatorem" is an uncertain reading of the scan and should be checked against "le-gatorem"/"leg-atorem"; the scan shows "le-" then "gatorem". The text "Galenus 2. de tem-" is continued by "per." at the foot right, which is the catchword.
